caps.cap: Hi there. In this lesson we'll read the gamepad's sticks.
We'll write four lines of code, and watch the numbers in AdvantageScope.
First, left-click to open the lessons folder.
These are the starters, one for each lesson.
Left-click L020SticksOpMode, once.
And copy it: ⌘C on a Mac, Ctrl+C on Windows and Ubuntu.
Left-click to fold the lessons folder back up.
Now left-click the mytry folder...
...and paste: ⌘V on a Mac, Ctrl+V on Windows and Ubuntu.
A Copy Class box opens, and the package already ends in mytry.
Left-click OK.
Android Studio asks to add the new file to Git.
Left-click Add.
Go to the top of the file: ⌘Home on a Mac, Ctrl+Home on Windows and Ubuntu.
Our own copy, open and ready. Its first line ends in mytry.
Find the line that says @Disabled, and left-click on it.
Delete the whole line: ⌘Delete on a Mac, Ctrl+Y on Windows and Ubuntu.
Gone. Now the robot will list our copy.
Scroll down to readTheSticks(), and left-click at the end of this step's comment.
Press Enter, and type: double leftStickY = gamepad1.
A list opens with everything a gamepad has.
Type left_st...
...and the list shrinks to the left stick.
left_stick_y is already picked. Press Tab.
Then a semicolon, to end the line.
No red underline. Good news. There's no syntax errors.
Hold the pointer still over left_stick_y...
...and a box says what it is: the left stick, up and down.
Move the pointer away, and left-click back in the editor.
Next step. Press Enter, and type Track.
There's more than one Tracker. The one from base is at the top.
Press Tab.
Then finish the line: Tracker.publish("stick/leftY", leftStickY);
Tracker isn't red, and an import line appeared at the top.
Scroll up: import org.firstinspires.ftc.teamcode.base.Tracker; is new. Then scroll back down.
Time to run it. Plug the gamepad into the laptop.
Left-click the Terminal button.
